findings.title: Sidebar shows raw router id, not label
findings.problem: assistant.llm_model_type is resolved to a display label via appInfoStore.findLLMLabel, which only searches this.llmModels (appInfo.ts:401-404) and never the new this.llmRouters list this diff introduces. LLMSelector.tsx now lets a router be saved as an assistant's llm_model_type, so that value falls through findLLMLabel's fallback.
findings.impact: The assistant details sidebar shows the router's raw slug (e.g. 'smart-router') instead of its friendly label for any assistant configured with a router as its LLM; AssistantDetailsSidebarSections.test.tsx mocks findLLMLabel entirely, so no test exercises real resolution and this ships silently.
findings.recommendation: Extend findLLMLabel (or add a sibling resolver) to also search appInfoStore.llmRouters before falling back to the raw value.

findings.title: Implicit default fallback can silently pick a router
findings.problem: defaultLlmModel falls back to models[0] when no model has isDefault true. models is llmModels concatenated with llmRouters, so when llmModels is empty but llmRouters is not, models[0] is a router, silently becoming the 'Default: <label>' option.
findings.impact: The effect at line 202 calls onChange(defaultLlmModel?.value) for any empty/invalid value, auto-selecting that router as the assistant's LLM with no explicit user choice or backend default signal — a router becomes the implicit default purely by array position.
findings.recommendation: Exclude routers from the implicit-default fallback, e.g. models.find(m => !m.isRouter) ?? models[0], or define an explicit rule for the empty-llmModels case.

findings.title: Temperature cap validation ignores router-routed models
findings.problem: getTemperatureMax looks up modelValue only in appInfoStore.llmModels; when modelValue is a router (now a valid llm_model_type per this diff), the store lookup misses and falls through to a name-based regex match against the router's own slug, not against any of its tiers' target models.
findings.impact: A router whose tiers route to Claude on a capped provider (aws_bedrock/google_vertexai/vertex_ai-anthropic_models) never matches /claude/i on its own slug, so the 1.0 temperature cap is silently skipped; a user can set temperature above 1.0 for an assistant that ultimately routes to Claude, risking a rejected/failed backend call.
findings.recommendation: Decide how a router should be validated — e.g. resolve its tiers and apply the strictest matching rule among them, or apply the Claude cap defensively whenever the model is a router. This needs a product decision on intended semantics for multi-tier routers before an unambiguous fix can be written.

findings.title: Chat router rows lack a visual Router indicator
findings.problem: renderOption's router branch passes only label, isPremium and selected into ModelOptionRow — no isRouter prop exists on ModelOptionRow at all — whereas this same diff extended LLMSelector.tsx's sibling row component (LlmOptionRow) with a dedicated blue 'Router' meta line for the identical concept.
findings.impact: A router row in the chat prompt dropdown renders identically to a model row and has no marker of its own; it relies entirely on sitting under the 'Routers' section header, which is easy to lose once the header scrolls out of view or during a search.
findings.recommendation: Add an isRouter prop to ModelOptionRow (mirroring LlmOptionRow's meta-line treatment) and pass it from the router branch of renderOption.

findings.title: Premium tip never fires for a premium router
findings.problem: effectiveModel is resolved via llmModels.find(...) only; it never consults llmRouters, even though ChatPromptLlmSelector.tsx (this same diff) already lets a router be saved as currentChat.llmModel and itself uses the exact llmModels-then-llmRouters fallback pattern this hook is missing.
findings.impact: When a premium router drives the chat, effectiveModel resolves to null, isPremiumActive is false, and every premium-cost indicator sourced from this hook (ChatPrompt's prompt ring, ChatPremiumModelTipSlot's dismissible tip, ChatHistory's visibility flag) silently stays off even though a premium router is actually driving the chat and its cost.
findings.recommendation: Add the same fallback already used in ChatPromptLlmSelector.tsx: llmModels.find(...) ?? llmRouters.find((r) => r.value === currentChat.llmModel) ?? null.

findings.title: Router card grid missing required md:grid-cols-2 breakpoint
findings.problem: The spec calls for the router-card grid to be grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 (two columns on wider viewports); the implementation uses grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 with no md: breakpoint.
findings.impact: Router cards always stack one-per-row regardless of viewport width, deviating from the approved spec's responsive layout requirement.
findings.recommendation: Add the md:grid-cols-2 class to the router cards' grid container.

findings.title: Unguarded router tier access can crash the catalog page
findings.problem: LLMRouterOption.tiers is typed as a required RouterTiers object with all four tier keys mandatory, but appInfo.ts:349-359 copies it straight from the untyped v1/llm_models response (tiers: router.tiers) with no runtime validation. RoutersSection.tsx's TIER_ORDER.map then does router.tiers[tier] and immediately reads tierModel.label with no null guard.
findings.impact: A router entry missing a tier key (or missing tiers altogether) throws a TypeError reading 'label' of undefined while rendering, crashing the Models Catalog page for every user until the backend payload is corrected — a defensive-coding gap with nothing protecting against a payload that violates the TS-only contract.
findings.recommendation: Guard the tier lookup, e.g. const tierModel = router.tiers?.[tier]; if (!tierModel) return null, and/or validate the tiers shape when mapping the API response in appInfo.ts.

findings.title: Router 'default' flag from backend is discarded
findings.problem: The raw v1/llm_models payload can mark any entry default: true the same way for models and routers, but routerEntries.map (appInfo.ts:349-360) never reads that flag onto LLMRouterOption, and LLMSelector.tsx hardcodes isDefault: false for every router folded into its combined models list.
findings.impact: If the backend ever marks a router as the default LLM, that intent is silently discarded end-to-end — no code path lets a router become the resolved default model in any selector.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether routers should participate in the 'default' concept at all (the spec's acceptance criteria never addressed it); if yes, thread router.default through LLMRouterOption and the selectors' isDefault comparisons. This needs product confirmation before an unambiguous fix is written.
